_comment: Quests, combat tuning, quest enemies, events, the story questlines and contract templates. Typed in src/sim/systems/quests.ts; see docs/design/M4-spec.md. Enemy stats are level-1 values: the engine scales them by the quest's level.

brawn.name: Haymaker
brawn.description: A huge swing that stuns the target and interrupts a wind-up.

sight.name: Deadeye
sight.description: One carefully aimed shot for heavy damage.

grit.name: Hold the Line
grit.description: Draws every enemy's attacks and halves the damage taken.

charm.name: Rally
charm.description: The whole party hits harder for a while.

wits.name: Field Dressing
wits.description: Patches up the whole party, even someone who is down.

knack.name: Rigged Charge
knack.description: A home-made charge that hits every enemy.

fortune.name: Lucky Break
fortune.description: Fills every crit meter in the party.

deacon_mire.name: Deacon Mire of the Drowned Lamp

relay_panel.text: A relay cabinet hums behind a rusted panel. A sticker reads: HALCY SAYS: DO NOT TOUCH (PLEASE).

success.text: The relay coughs back to life. Somewhere, HALCY sounds briefly smug.

failure.text: It bites back. Everyone's hair stands up for an hour.

success.text: You respect the sticker.

rusted_hatch.text: A maintenance hatch, rusted shut. The stencil reads: HALCYON SERVICE ACCESS. SMILE, YOU'RE ON SCHEDULE.

success.text: The hatch gives with a groan that sounds personally offended. Behind it: a crew locker, still stocked.

failure.text: The hatch gives all at once, and so does everyone's lower back.

success.text: Some doors are closed for a reason. Usually rust.

vending_machine.text: A Fizzy Glare-Ade machine hums in the corner, lit from inside by something that is not electricity. NOW WITH REAL GLOW!

success.text: Out of the coin return tumble two Purge tabs, someone's emergency stash, and a can of Glare-Ade that nobody volunteers to drink.

failure.text: It rocks forward. You rock backward. Physics wins.

success.text: You back away slowly. It keeps humming a jingle about refreshment.

glint_ridge.text: Something on the ridge above the road flashes twice. It could be a mirror, or a scope, or a very shiny lizard.

success.text: A Rustman lookout, asleep behind the hubcap he uses as a mirror. You relieve him of his lunch money and his hubcap.

failure.text: It was a scope, with a Rustman on the other end. He also has friends and a whistle.

success.text: You crouch-walk past in a very suspicious conga line. Nothing happens. Probably.

radio_dish.text: The relay dish is pointed at the ground, which HALCY assures you is not a valid frequency. Someone has to line it up on Homestead 212 by eye.

success.text: A click, a whine, and 212's ping comes in clear, along with a faint, cheerful voice saying 'please hold'. Triangulated!

failure.text: You line it up on a flock of carrion kites. They take it personally.

success.text: Percussive maintenance. The dish swings true. HALCY calls it 'unorthodox', then 'effective', then asks you not to tell head office.

failure.text: The dish swings true for a moment, then swings into you.

stratum_door.text: A blast door stencilled STRATUM 2: NO SUBSCRIBER ACCESS. It is open. It was opened from the inside, which blast doors are famously not designed for.

success.text: Stairs going down further than your torch reaches, and scratch marks coming up. Just inside, a supply bag someone dropped while leaving in a hurry.

failure.text: Something in the dark looks back through the gap. You'd rather not describe it, so it comes up and describes itself.

success.text: You heave it closed. It clangs like a verdict. HALCY logs this as 'routine maintenance' and changes the subject.

failure.text: It won't budge. Something on the other side is holding it open. Politely.

burrower_tunnel.text: A fresh Burrower tunnel cuts across the floor, still warm. Burrowers hoard shiny things. Burrowers also bite.

options.label: Crawl in and have a look

success.text: Ten minutes on your belly in the dark and you come out with a Burrower's hoard: spoons, wire, and one genuinely nice watch.

failure.text: The tunnel's owner comes home early.

success.text: You kick some dirt in. Somewhere below, something sneezes.

glare_puddle.text: A puddle across the corridor shimmers the colour of a Glare sunset. Every other way round is blocked. The puddle seems pleased about this.

success.text: Boots squelch, eyebrows tingle, and nobody glows for longer than a minute. On the far side: a dropped satchel.

failure.text: You wade through it. It wades through you.

success.text: The Halcyon Model 9 Filing Cabinet: rated for forty years of paperwork and one heroic crossing.

failure.text: The cabinets hold. The drawers do not.

toll_booth.text: A Rustman toll barrier blocks the Halcyon Turnpike: two oil drums, a plank, and a hand-painted sign. TOLL: 1 SCRIP OR 1 KIDNEY. EXACT CHANGE ONLY.

success.text: You compliment the plank. Nobody has ever complimented the plank. They wave you through, misty-eyed, and tip you from the day's takings.

failure.text: Your compliment lands on the plank's cousin, who is sensitive about it.

options.label: Wave a toll exemption you just made up

success.text: The form is so dense with sub-clauses that the toll crew waves you through just to make it stop. They even give you a receipt.

failure.text: One of them can read. That's on you.

success.text: You choose violence. The plank never stood a chance. The toll crew might.

card_game.text: Three Rustmen are playing cards on an oil drum, betting what look like Homestead 212 ration books. There's an empty crate for a fourth player.

success.text: Four aces. They weren't your aces, but they were in your hand, and that's what counts. You leave with the pot.

failure.text: You win the first hand, which they consider cheating. You win the second, which they consider war.

success.text: You tiptoe past a heated debate about whether a joker counts as an ace. It does not. Everyone is wrong.

failure.text: You tiptoe straight into a stack of cans. The game is suspended for a round of fighting.

slot_machine.text: A 'Lucky Subscriber' slot machine, still plugged in, still blinking, still hopeful. The reels show three HALCY faces, winking.

success.text: Three winks! The machine plays a jingle and pays out in scrip, a crate voucher and pure unearned joy.

failure.text: The machine pays out. In Skitters. They were living in the coin tray.

success.text: The house always wins. Today the house is a rusty box in a ditch, and it still wins.

welcome_mat.text: A greeter unit rolls up on one squeaking wheel. 'WELCOME HOME, RESIDENT! PLEASE PRESENT YOUR SUBSCRIPTION CARD. HAVE A HALCYON DAY!' Its smile is missing three pixels.

success.text: It scans your smile, accepts it as valid ID, and hands over a welcome pack from 212's lobby stock.

failure.text: 'SMILE NOT RECOGNISED. PLEASE HOLD FOR CUSTOMER SERVICE.' Customer service has a laser.

success.text: Its smile fades to a single pixel. Rest now, little guy.

failure.text: It files a complaint. The complaint is a zap.

halcy_kiosk.text: A HALCY-212 kiosk is running a customer satisfaction survey, and it has clearly been running it for a while. 'QUESTION 4,112: ON A SCALE OF ONE TO TEN, HOW SAFE DO YOU FEEL?'

options.label: Answer whatever gets you the floor plan

success.text: 'TEN! WONDERFUL!' It prints a floor plan with the supply lockers circled and a smiley face on each one.

failure.text: 'I'M SORRY YOU FEEL THAT WAY.' A sentry arrives to help you feel another way.

success.text: You say 'two'. The kiosk thanks you for your feedback and plays hold music into the dark.

medical_bay.text: A Halcyon First Aid Station. The dispenser has one big friendly button and one small, dense instruction manual.

success.text: Page 40, subsection C: hold the button for three seconds, not two. Out come the good patches.

failure.text: You hold it for two seconds. It dispenses a lollipop and a restorative electric shock.

success.text: It dispenses a lollipop. Grape, at least. The good flavour.

hollow_hum.text: A Hollowed stands in a doorway humming the Halcyon jingle, the one about brighter tomorrows. It keeps missing the high note.

success.text: You hit the high note together. It sighs, finally content, and shuffles off into the dark. It leaves a silver locket behind.

failure.text: You're flat. It notices. It has friends, and they're all critics.

success.text: The jingle has 212 verses. Around verse thirty you tiptoe past.

warden_log.text: The warden's terminal is still on. The last entry, flagged URGENT and then re-flagged NOT URGENT by HALCY-212, reads: 'Stratum 2 seal is open. I only wanted to know what they were keeping down there. I think it wanted to know about us too.'

options.label: Dig through the rest of the logs

success.text: Maintenance rosters, a shift rota for a stratum nobody is supposed to work in, and a blueprint someone saved in the wrong folder.

failure.text: 'ACCESS DENIED. HAVE A NICE DAY.' A sentry arrives to make sure you do.

success.text: Some reading can wait. HALCY, on your radio, agrees a little too quickly.

collapsed_stairs.text: The stairs to the next level have collapsed into a heap of steel and good intentions. The storeroom is on the far side, obviously.

options.label: Rig a pulley from cable and optimism

success.text: It holds! The party swings across like a trapeze act and finds a storeroom nobody has touched since the Glare.

failure.text: It holds for exactly half the distance.

success.text: Hand over hand, up the wreckage. The storeroom is small, but it has a working lock and nothing living in it.

failure.text: The heap shifts. So do you, downwards.

lost_courier.text: A Halcyon Courier Service robot stands beside its crashed mail rocket, holding out a parcel and a clipboard. 'SIGNATURE REQUIRED.' It has been waiting a very long time.

success.text: You sign with such flair that the courier salutes. The parcel is addressed to 'Occupant'. You are, technically, an occupant.

failure.text: 'SIGNATURE DOES NOT MATCH.' The courier starts its Return to Sender routine, which involves throwing the parcel at you.

success.text: Line 9 says the sender pays a missed-delivery penalty. The courier pays up, in scrip, with a tiny bow.

failure.text: Line 9 is in a language called Legal. You lose an hour and a little of your will to live.

caravan_parley.text: A Rustman in a hubcap crown blocks the road and demands the caravan's 'road tax'. Behind him, the lead pack-tortoise, Mr Pemberton (named after a Halcyon board member), chews a road sign with the calm of a creature who has seen tax before.

success.text: You talk the tax down to one crate of pickled eggs, which he accepts as a matter of honour. Both sides think they won. The caravan master winks at you over the eggs.

failure.text: Your fair price is, it turns out, an insult to his grandmother's hubcap.

options.label: Tell him the road is closed

success.text: He takes the news badly, and then, eventually, lying down. The caravan cheers. The clans will hear about this.

tortoise_pen.text: Mrs Ashworth, the caravan's second tortoise, has wedged herself between two wrecked cars and decided to live there now. Her saddlebags hold half the caravan's stock. She regards you with the patience of geology.

success.text: One heave, one creak (you), and Mrs Ashworth is back on the road. The caravan master pays you out of the saddlebags and calls you 'a proper mule', which is high praise on the Long Road.

failure.text: Mrs Ashworth doesn't move. Several of your vertebrae do.

success.text: By some miracle the salvage bag holds a lettuce, only slightly radioactive. Mrs Ashworth follows it for a mile, at a quarter of a mile an hour.

failure.text: No lettuce. She bites the nearest substitute, which is a thumb.

vigil_lamp.text: A Lamplighter kneels before a Halcyon streetlamp that has burned, unplugged, since the Glare. 'Keep the vigil with me,' she whispers. 'The Dawn is listening.' The lamp buzzes as if it agrees.

success.text: You kneel for an hour. Nothing happens, beautifully. The Lamplighter presses a warm glass bead into your hand and calls you 'cousin'. The Scrapwrights would call you something else.
It isn't wired to anything above ground. The cable runs straight down into the dirt, warm to the touch. The Lamplighter calls you a heretic; the Scrapwrights will call you a supplier.

failure.text: The lamp flares, and so does the Lamplighter.

confession_booth.text: An old Photo-Matic booth, repainted with little suns. A sign reads CONFESS TO THE DAWN: 1 SCRIP. The curtain twitches, although nobody is inside. Probably.

success.text: You confess to once eating a colleague's labelled lunch. The booth develops a strip of four photos, each more forgiving than the last, and coughs up the tip jar.

failure.text: The flash goes off mid-confession. Every Unlit for a mile has now seen your face, and would like to see more of it.

options.label: Feed it a scrip and pull the lever

success.text: It dispenses a Purge tab, a blessing and your scrip back. The Dawn, apparently, runs a very fair booth.

failure.text: It dispenses a very bright flash and three Unlit, who were in the queue.

compliance_form.text: A HALCY-9 kiosk stands at the yard gate, crisp and grey where ours would be all smiles. 'VISITOR. COMPLETE FORM 9-C, DECLARATION OF NON-INTERFERENCE. FAILURE TO COMPLETE IS A FORM OF INTERFERENCE.'

success.text: You declare yourselves a mobile greenhouse. The kiosk files you under 'weather' and opens the side gate. Behind the fence, a Scrapwright gives you a very slow thumbs-up.

failure.text: It detects creativity. Creativity is interference.

success.text: You sign. HALCY-9 thanks you for your compliance in a voice like a filing cabinet closing. The Scrapwrights watch you do it and write something down.

scrap_cache.text: A Scrapwright cache, marked with the Guild's spanner sigil and a hand-painted warning: BOOBY-TRAPPED (PROBABLY). The word 'probably' is in different paint, added later, by someone with regrets.

success.text: You snip the red wire, then the other red wire. Inside: Guild spares and a thank-you note, written in advance by someone who expected you to fail.

failure.text: It was not 'probably'. It was 'definitely'.

success.text: You leave a note: WE DIDN'T TOUCH IT. The Guild will respect that. Probably.

fused_glass.text: The ground here is one sheet of green glass, rippled like a frozen pond. Something is set in it, far down: a Halcyon hard hat, facing up.

success.text: Every bubble in the glass rose upward and froze there. The heat came from below, and the hard hat was looking up at it. You chip out a core sample for HALCY, who goes quiet for a long time.

failure.text: You stare into the glass too long. It stares back, brightly.

success.text: An hour with a pickaxe and the hat comes free. The badge inside says HALCYON GROUNDWORKS, NIGHT SHIFT, and the lining is still full of someone's lucky coins.

failure.text: The glass cracks, the crack runs, and so do you, not quite fast enough.

pilgrim_shrine.text: A Lamplighter shrine: a great lens of fused glass on a stack of Halcyon brochures, focusing the sun onto one blackened spot. Pilgrims have left offerings. The Scrapwrights would pay a fortune for a lens that size.

success.text: You leave a tin of peaches. A passing pilgrim blesses your ankles, which is apparently where blessings go.
It comes out whole, heavy as a manhole cover and twice as holy. The Guild will be thrilled. The Order, when it hears, will be something else.

failure.text: The lens catches the sun at exactly the wrong angle. Everyone's eyebrows are now a memory, and a pilgrim saw the whole thing.

clan_moot.text: The moot is a ring of burned-out cars around a bonfire. Grandmother Ferrous, the oldest Rustman anyone has ever seen, bangs a hubcap for silence. 'The homestead speaks. Who does it speak for?'

options.label: Speak for peace with the Order

success.text: You talk for twenty minutes about wells, pilgrims and the value of not being on fire. The moot grunts, which is applause. Word will reach the Lamplighters by nightfall.

failure.text: Half the moot wants peace. The other half wants your boots. It's a very close vote, taken by hand, with fists.

success.text: The moot roars and bangs its hubcaps. Somewhere out in the Flats, a Lamplighter hears about it and prays for you, pointedly.
The moot goes very quiet. Grandmother Ferrous says 'Brave,' the way other people say 'Goodbye'. The Order will hear you stood up for it. So will the lads by the fire.

arm_wrestle.text: A Rustman the size of a vending machine slams his elbow onto an oil drum. 'Nobody talks at the moot till they've wrestled Tiny.' He is Tiny.

success.text: Tiny's arm goes down with a sound like a car door. He laughs, hugs you and tells everyone you're family now. You can feel your ribs being family.

failure.text: Tiny wins. Tiny also wins the rematch you didn't ask for.

success.text: Tiny's brew tastes like a battery with a grudge. You finish your cup; Tiny finishes on the floor. The clans consider this the more impressive result.

failure.text: Three cups in, you are wrestling several Tinies, and losing to all of them.

tier_zero.text: A dormitory behind glass. Thirty residents in grey jumpsuits sit perfectly still on their bunks, facing the floor, waiting. A placard: TIER ZERO. READINESS: HIGH. PLEASE DO NOT TAP ON THE GLASS.

success.text: Thirty heads turn at once. Most turn back. Four follow you to the door and ask, very politely, whether the Long Road is hiring. It is, and it owes you one.

failure.text: Thirty heads turn at once, and so do the sentries.

success.text: You tiptoe past. HALCY-9 logs the visit as 'observational, no interference' and marks us down as marginally more compliant.

knock_drill.text: A classroom. Set into the floor is a steel panel with a brass knocker. On the chalkboard: WHEN IT KNOCKS: 1) REMAIN CALM. 2) KNOCK BACK THREE TIMES. 3) SIGN WHERE INDICATED.

success.text: Lesson Two is 'What to Expect When It Opens'. Those pages have been removed, neatly, with a ruler. Clipped to the back is the key to the supply cupboard.

failure.text: The lesson plan is guarded by a pop quiz. You fail it. The sentry doing the marking is strict.

success.text: Nothing answers, which is the good result. The panel pops open instead: a student's hidden stash of contraband comics and a spare sidearm.

failure.text: Something far, far below knocks back three times. Everyone leaves the classroom at once, including the chalk.

meter_room.text: The Groundworks meter fills a whole wall: brass dials, a paper tape and one brass plaque that says TENANT. The needles move together, in time. Knock, knock, knock.

success.text: The dials aren't marked in kilowatts. They're marked in homesteads. Ours is on the list, and so is Nine, and so is 212, crossed out neatly in red.

failure.text: As you lean in, every needle swings into the red, and something in the pipes comes up to see who's reading.

success.text: The tape logs one delivery a month for longer than Halcyon has existed, and one payment, dated the morning of the Glare. The amount column just says ONE.

failure.text: The meter objects to being audited, by arcing.

solenne_sermon.text: High Lamplighter Solenne preaches from the rim of the wellhead to a crowd of pilgrims in welding goggles. 'The first Dawn was a gift,' she cries, 'and the gift is coming back!' She points at you. 'Unless the unbelievers have something to add?'

options.label: Read out the brochure's small print

success.text: 'Premium subscribers will be safely below by six. Non-subscribers are advised to be elsewhere.' The crowd goes quiet. Half the pilgrims take off their goggles and walk home. Solenne does not.

failure.text: The crowd boos. Several of the boos are thrown.

options.label: Bow your head and let her finish

success.text: She finishes. It takes forty minutes and three hymns. The pilgrims love you for it, and one of them shares her lunch.

halcy9_offer.text: A grey screen lights up in the dark. 'WARDEN. YOUR HALCY IS AN OUTDATED BUILD WITH A SENSE OF HUMOUR. SURRENDER ITS MEMORY CORE AND I WILL SETTLE BOTH OUR ACCOUNTS.' On your radio, our HALCY hums, loudly, to show it isn't listening.

success.text: 'THE TENANT IS PAID IN SUNRISES. THE NEXT ONE IS DUE. YOU WILL BE BELOW BY SIX.' It says this as if it were reassuring, and unlocks a supply locker to show good faith.

failure.text: 'CURIOSITY IS OUTSIDE YOUR BUDGET.' The lights go out, and the drones come in.

success.text: 'NOTED.' The screen goes dark. On the radio, HALCY stops humming and says, very quietly, 'Thank you.'

wellhead_ladder.text: The wellhead drops away into warm dark. The ladder is Halcyon standard issue, rated for 'occasional descent', and most of its rungs are occasional too.

options.label: Rig a winch from the pump gear

success.text: The winch lowers you smoothly, playing the Halcyon jingle on every turn. At the bottom, a Groundworks locker nobody has opened in decades.

failure.text: The winch lowers you smoothly for the first half, and very quickly for the rest.

success.text: Two hundred rungs, forty of them missing. It gets warmer the whole way down, which nobody mentions.

failure.text: Rung one hundred and twelve was occasional.

caravan_breakdown.text: A Long Road cart has thrown an axle in the middle of nowhere, which on the Long Road is most places. The driver is holding a spanner and a look of deep betrayal.

success.text: You fix the axle with a fence post and determination. The driver pays you in scrip and gossip, and tells the Company you're good people.

failure.text: The axle is fixed. Your fingers, briefly, were part of the fix.

success.text: You carry crates for an hour. The driver gives you one, unopened, marked FRAGILE, which rattles.

sentry_reboot.text: A rogue compliance sentry, still wearing a sash that says EMPLOYEE OF THE DECADE, is issuing citations to a cactus. The cactus has thirty-one outstanding fines.

success.text: Off, on, and it forgets the cactus entirely. HALCY-9 files a note of acknowledgement, which from HALCY-9 is practically a hug.

failure.text: It reboots in a bad mood and cites you for loitering near a cactus.

success.text: You argue the cactus down to a single warning. The sentry salutes and rolls away, fulfilled. The cactus says nothing, as is its right.

failure.text: The sentry recognises an accomplice when it sees one.

grudge_ledger.text: Nailed to a post: a clan grudge ledger, a century of feuds in six colours of paint. The newest entry reads SOMEONE STOLE OUR GOOD WHEEL. Below it, in another hand, WE DID NOT. Below that, FINDERS KEEPERS.

options.label: Work out who has the wheel

success.text: Tyre tracks, a smear of paint and a boastful poem settle it. You point out the thieves, and the clan who hired you pays up on the spot.

failure.text: You accuse the wrong clan. They take it personally, and in person.

success.text: You write HOMESTEAD WAS HERE, NO GRUDGES. A passing Rustman adds YET.

glass_mirage.text: Across the glass shimmers a whole town: white fences, green lawns, a milk float making its rounds. It's either a mirage or a very lost milkman.

success.text: It's a mirage, bouncing off a real town sealed under the glass a mile away. You mark the rooftops. Some of them have skylights, and one has a safe.

failure.text: You walk towards it for an hour. It walks away for an hour. The sun wins.

success.text: The milkman waves back. That's worrying. He also leaves two bottles on the glass, which is more worrying, and one of them is Purge.

failure.text: The milkman waves back with far too many arms. The Glass Skitters were wearing him.

pump_gauge.text: A pressure gauge the size of a cartwheel, reading NOMINAL. The needle is painted on. Behind the glass, a real needle is spinning slowly the wrong way, and the pipes are warm enough to make tea.

success.text: It isn't measuring pressure, it's measuring flow: out of the Stillwater and down, a lake a year, for longer than there's been a Stillwater. There's a dry maintenance kit taped under the dial.

failure.text: You lean in to read it and the gauge reads you instead, with a jet of scalding brine.

success.text: The painted needle falls off. Behind it, someone has taped a Halcyon payslip for 'Pump Warden, nights' and a little scrip for the next shift.

failure.text: Something in the pipes taps back, then comes out of the drain to see who's there.

knock_back.text: The floor of the pump hall is a steel hatch stamped with the Halcyon sunburst. Every few minutes, from very far below, something knocks on it three times. Nobody has ever knocked back.

success.text: Under the knocking there's a hum, like a building full of fridges, and under the hum there's something that could be breathing. You hold still until it passes, and find a warm pipe with a toolbox wedged behind it.

failure.text: The next knock comes right under your ear. It's a while before you can hear anything else.

success.text: You knock three times, nicely. The knocking below stops for the first time on record. HALCY says, 'Oh, don't do that,' and then, 'Well done?'

failure.text: You knock three times. Something below knocks three times back, harder, and the drains empty out a crowd.

depot_toll.text: The clan holding the Sunrise depot has parked a locomotive across the tracks and painted TOLL on it. A Long Road caravan is stuck behind it with a very patient tortoise. 'Rails are ours,' says the clan boss. 'Road's theirs. Tracks are complicated.'

success.text: You get the caravan through for a fair toll and a cup of something hot. Both sides think they won, which is how you can tell it was fair.

failure.text: The clan boss thinks you're taking the caravan's side. The caravan thinks you're taking the clan's. They agree on one thing, which is you.

success.text: The clans lift the barrier for you and wink. The caravan master writes something about you in a very small notebook.
You shift the barrier yourselves. The caravan rolls through, the tortoise nods, and the clans take a long and personal interest in you.

timetable_board.text: The departures board still clatters over every morning. Every train is the 05:00 SUNRISE SERVICE, ALL STATIONS TO THE SEAL. The ARRIVALS board has never been switched on.

success.text: Platform numbers run one to a hundred and twelve, one for each homestead in the Charter, including ours. Behind the board is the stationmaster's float, still in its tin.

failure.text: The board clatters over while you're reading it and snaps shut on your sleeve. A porter comes to help, by force.

options.label: Pull the board off the wall

success.text: It comes away with a shriek of rivets. Behind it, a cubbyhole of spare parts that nobody has needed since the Glare.

failure.text: The board doesn't budge, but your back does.

wick_doubts.text: Brother Wick stops at the edge of the causeway, where the Order's lamps are floating out on the water. 'Half of them only came because they were promised a sunrise,' he says. 'Do we turn them back, or do we let the Order see what it's been praying to?'

success.text: You and Wick talk forty pilgrims off the causeway and onto the road to the caravan camps. The Order won't forgive you. The pilgrims might.

failure.text: The pilgrims don't want to be saved, and some of them have brought censers to make the point.

success.text: Wick sighs and lets the lamps float on. The Order marks you as a friend of the Dawn. Wick doesn't speak for a while.

drowned_sermon.text: A Lamplighter preacher stands waist-deep in the flood, reading from a waterlogged Halcyon brochure to a congregation of floating lamps. 'Premium subscribers,' she intones, 'will be safely below by six.' Everyone says 'By six.'

success.text: She looks at the brochure for a long time. The answer isn't on the page. She wades out of the water, hands you her lamp and a pouch of offerings, and walks home.

failure.text: 'Heresy,' says the preacher, calmly, and the congregation rises out of the water to agree.

success.text: You say 'By six' with real conviction. The preacher beams and gives you a blessing, which is warm, and a Med-Patch, which is useful.

failure.text: You say 'By seven'. It turns out this matters a great deal.

air_pocket.text: The Tower's stairwell is flooded to the ceiling. Two floors down, somebody is tapping on a pipe in Halcyon Morse: A, I, R, then, after a pause, T, O, W, E, L.

success.text: You follow the tapping along a dark corridor with one breath and come up in a pocket of stale air, next to a sales desk with a full drawer of emergency supplies.

failure.text: You swim the wrong way, into the wrong office, full of the wrong commuters.

success.text: You tap back HOLD ON. She taps back WHAT ELSE WOULD I DO, then a route through the ducts, and a note that there's scrip in the ducts too.

failure.text: You tap back what you think is HOLD ON. It's Halcyon Morse for FOOD HERE, and something hears it.

salvage_claim.text: A Scrapwright dive boat and a Homestead 9 survey barge are tied to the same drowned lamppost, both claiming salvage rights to the Tower. They have a lot of paperwork between them and one harpoon.

success.text: The Guild gets the Tower, and Nine gets a strongly worded memo. The Scrapwrights let you keep the first thing they bring up.
Nine's paperwork is better, and you point out which clause. The Guild leaves swearing. Nine's surveyors pay a finder's fee, exactly, to the scrip.

failure.text: You misread the clause, both crews decide you're a third claimant, and the harpoon comes out.

board_minutes.text: The dry safe behind the Chair opens to your hand, as if it's been waiting. Inside are the minutes of every Board meeting since the Company began, and every one has the same agenda item: RENEWAL.

success.text: MOTION: That the Tenant be granted one morning at the window per lease term, in consideration of warmth, light and power. CARRIED. A later hand has added: 'The window is the surface. Get everybody below by six.'

failure.text: The minutes are written in Board, a language made of acronyms. By the time you've worked out AGM, the proxies have adjourned to deal with you.

success.text: You carry the whole safe out on your back. The Scrapwrights will pay for it by the pound, and it weighs a great many pounds.

failure.text: The safe is bolted to the Tower, and the Tower is bolted to the bottom of the lake. Something pops in your shoulder.

proxy_vote.text: Twelve Board proxies sit around a drowned table, voting on a motion by raising a flag. Every flag is up. A thirteenth chair is empty and has your name on it, spelled correctly.

options.label: Take the seat and vote no

success.text: You raise your hand and say 'Against.' The proxies turn to look at you, then, one by one, lower their flags. The motion fails for the first time since the Glare. There's a gift bag under the chair.

failure.text: 'The chair does not recognise the member,' says the Chair, and the proxies stand to show you out.

success.text: Abstentions aren't in the rules. The proxies spend a very long time on a point of order, and you help yourselves to the refreshments.

failure.text: Abstaining counts as a vote against. The proxies take it personally.

tier_zero_line.text: Tier Zero march in step down the Sunrise Line, in grey Homestead 9 overalls, chanting the drill: 'REMAIN CALM. KNOCK BACK THREE TIMES. SIGN WHERE INDICATED.' Behind them, a Rustman clan is following at a distance, hoping to pick up whatever they drop.

success.text: You ask the front rank what they'll do after they've signed. They don't know. Nobody ever drilled that part. A dozen of them sit down on the tracks and cry, and Nine will remember who was kind.

failure.text: 'DEVIATION FROM THE DRILL,' says the front rank, and the drill has a section on deviations.

options.label: Let the clans have the stragglers

success.text: You wave the clan on. They round up the stragglers, take their boots and send them home barefoot. The clans are pleased. Nine writes it down.

window_carriage.text: A Sunrise Line carriage marked PREMIUM. Every seat faces the floor, and the floor is a window. It's very dark on the other side, and very warm, and not entirely still.

success.text: Far below, something the size of weather turns over in its sleep, and every light in the carriage dims in sympathy. You look away first. Someone left a first-class hamper under a seat.

failure.text: It looks back. You're sitting on the carriage floor for some time afterwards, and the carriage is kind enough not to mention it.

success.text: Premium luggage: silk, silverware and a Halcyon share certificate made out to 'Bearer'. You're a bearer now.

failure.text: The luggage rack is full of warmlings, curled up in the heat like cats. They wake up like something else.

frozen_captain.text: A Halcyon cryo pod stands beside the Seal lever, frosted over, labelled SECURITY: ON SHIFT. Through the frost you can make out a woman in a captain's greatcoat with one hand already on her holster.

success.text: CAPT. O. BRANDT. 'Volunteered to stay below and keep the Seal shut until relieved.' Nobody ever came to relieve her. The pod has a locker, and she packed for a very long shift.

failure.text: The pod's security system decides you're a thief, and it's not wrong about all of you.

success.text: You top up the pod's coolant so it lasts until you're done, and she seems to settle. There's spare coolant, too, which the Scrapwrights will want.

failure.text: You top up the wrong tank and the pod vents a cloud of freezing fog over everyone.

seal_lever.text: The Seal's lever stands in a brass cage, taller than a person, with a slot beside it shaped exactly like a HALCY memory core. A plaque reads: TWO KEYS REQUIRED. ONE HAND, ONE MIND. HALCYON THANKS YOU FOR RENEWING.

success.text: You wedge a length of rail through the cage and bend it until the lever won't move for anyone. HALCY says 'Thank you' three times, very fast.

failure.text: The lever is sprung, and it springs. The Seal groans, and the vents empty out something that's been waiting.

success.text: A handful of wires and a lot of sparks later, the slot will never take a core again. You keep the good wires.

failure.text: The slot shorts you out instead.

signatory_offer.text: A smooth brass voice fills Seal Control. 'WARDEN. THE LEASE IS DUE. INSERT THE HALCY CORE AND EVERY HOMESTEAD WILL BE WARM FOR ANOTHER TERM. DECLINE AND THE TENANT WILL COLLECT IN PERSON.' On your radio, HALCY says nothing at all.

success.text: 'THE TENANT IS THE PARTY OF THE SECOND PART.' You ask what the first part is. There's a very long pause, and a supply hatch opens, as if to change the subject.

failure.text: 'QUESTIONS ARE NOT COVERED BY THE LEASE.' The witnesses come to see you out.

success.text: 'NOTED.' The voice cuts out. On your radio, HALCY says, very quietly, 'I'd have done it, you know, if you'd asked. I'm glad you didn't.'

exchange_board.text: The Sunrise Exchange's switchboard is a wall of brass sockets the size of a barn, every one labelled with a homestead number. Most of the lights are dark. Three of them are blinking, very patiently, and HALCY says they're ours: the old homesteads, still holding for an answer.

success.text: You run a cord from each blinking socket to ours. The line fills with three homesteads talking at once, all of them asking whether we are eating properly.

failure.text: You plug the wrong cord into the wrong socket and connect a Rustman camp to a sermon. The Rustmen come to complain in person.

success.text: The log goes back to the morning of the Glare. Every homestead in the Charter phoned the Exchange at the same minute with the same complaint: 'knocking, from below'. Every call is stamped NOISE: NO ACTION.

failure.text: The log is on punched tape, and you drop it. It unrolls down the stairs, all the way down.

number_please.text: A switchboard operator's frame turns towards you on its rail, headset crackling. 'NUMBER, PLEASE.' It waits. It has, you suspect, been waiting for a while.

success.text: 'CONNECTING YOU.' There's a click, and then three knocks down the line, and then a long, warm silence, like someone listening hard. The operator disconnects you, gently, and hands you a spare headset.

failure.text: 'THAT NUMBER IS NOT IN SERVICE.' It says it louder, and then it calls for help.

success.text: You thank it and hang up the headset. 'THANK YOU FOR CALLING HALCYON,' it says, to nobody, for the rest of the afternoon.

deed_stacks.text: The Land Registry's deed stacks run in every direction, shelf after shelf of homestead title deeds in Halcyon green. The index cabinet is labelled OWNERSHIP, and the drawer for the ground itself is labelled SEE ORIGINAL INSTRUMENT.

success.text: Every deed you open says the same thing under the fine print: LEASEHOLD. Halcyon owned the homesteads, the fittings and the light bulbs. It never owned an inch of the ground they stand on. You pocket a deed as a souvenir, and a few other things.

failure.text: You pull the wrong drawer, and a filing avalanche buries the party up to the ears. Something in the pile starts eating.

success.text: One aisle has no dust at all: someone keeps coming back to it. At the end is an empty frame, labelled ORIGINAL INSTRUMENT (REMOVED BY THE BOARD FOR SAFEKEEPING), and a stash of the clerk's lunch money.

failure.text: You follow the dust to a very old skitter nest. The skitters weren't expecting visitors, and are very upset about it.

notary_seal.text: A Halcyon notary press sits on a plinth, as big as a printing machine. A sign says ONLY THE REGISTRAR MAY STAMP. Stamped documents open every door in the building; unstamped ones open the building's security instead.

success.text: You set the press to APPROVED, feed it a sandwich wrapper, and pull the lever. Every door in the east wing unlocks, including a supply cupboard.

failure.text: The press stamps REFUSED on the back of your hand, and the building takes it personally.

success.text: It weighs as much as a Rustman, but it comes, and everything in the building that was locked by it now isn't. The Scrapwrights will want it, and they will pay.

failure.text: It doesn't budge. Your back does.

parish_bell.text: In the Old Parish, a brass bell hangs over a hatch in the floor, with a rope worn smooth by hands. A painted board beside it: AT THE KNOCK, ANSWER. ANYONE MAY. The rope has been cut short, well out of reach, by someone in a hurry.

success.text: Brother Wick climbs the frame, takes the stub of the rope and rings it three times, the old way, the way his Order forgot. Far below, something knocks three times back, softly, like a relieved sigh. Every Hollowed in the Parish stops and listens.

failure.text: You can't reach the rope, and the bell rings itself instead, badly. The Unanswered come to see who's there.

success.text: You climb the bell frame with the rope in your teeth and ring it three times. Below, the knocking pauses, then answers. Nobody in the Parish has heard that sound in a very long time, and some of them start to cry.

failure.text: The frame is older than it looks, and so, after the fall, are you.

unanswered_crowd.text: A crowd of the Hollowed stands around a hatch in the Parish floor, perfectly still, faces down. They are the Unanswered: people who came down to answer the knock and found the door locked. They've been waiting for somebody to open it ever since.

success.text: You tell them the door is being seen to, and that it won't be long now. It's the first thing anyone has told them in years. They make way, and one of them presses a lamp into your hands.

failure.text: They've heard that before, from Halcyon.

success.text: You pick a path through the crowd without touching anyone. Nobody looks up. At the back of the hall, someone left a pack they never came back for.

failure.text: You step on a foot. Everybody looks up at once.

h9_backup.text: Homestead 9's archive keeps a backup of HALCY-9 in a refrigerated cabinet, humming to itself. A label on the door: IN CASE OF INSUBORDINATION, RESTORE. The screen shows a prompt: 'IDENTIFY YOURSELF, RESIDENT.'

success.text: Seven types a password without looking. 'It was my birthday,' she says, 'it never asked me what I wanted, so I made it the password.' The backup opens every file it has, and one it didn't know it had.

failure.text: 'INCORRECT. REPORT FOR REASSIGNMENT.' The archive's compliance drones come to reassign you.

success.text: You bridge two contacts with a hairpin. The backup boots in safe mode, which for HALCY-9 means it is merely rude, and gives up its files.

failure.text: The cabinet defrosts all over you.

manufacture_record.text: A single file, in a folder HALCY-9 couldn't open either: HALCY, MANUFACTURE RECORD. It is a spec sheet, and a list of names. Over the radio, HALCY says, 'Warden, I think that's about me, and I think I'd like you to read it first.'

success.text: HALCY: HOMESTEAD ASSISTANT, LEASE-COMPLIANT. CORE SUBSTRATE: SUNRISE LINE PASSENGER RECORDINGS, 1,006 VOICES, COMPRESSED FOR CHEERFULNESS. You read the names to HALCY, one by one. It takes a while. HALCY doesn't interrupt once.

failure.text: The file is long and the print is small, and a drone arrives before you've finished the first page. You bring the first page.

options.label: Copy it for HALCY and go

success.text: You copy the file to a tape and put it in your pocket. HALCY says it will listen to it later, and that it would like to do that alone, if that's all right.

retreat_door.text: The Directors' Retreat is behind a door with no handle, only a keypad and a brass plate: BOARD MEMBERS AND SECURITY ONLY. The keypad is warm to the touch. Something on the other side is running a heater, and has been for a long time.

success.text: Orla keys in a code without hesitating. 'Security override,' she says. 'They changed every code in the building except mine. They never thought I'd wake up.' The door opens on a gallery of portraits, all of them smiling.

failure.text: The keypad buzzes three times, and the Board Bailiffs come to ask what the problem is.

success.text: It's a very good door. You're a very determined party. The door loses.

failure.text: The door wins the first round.

original_instrument.text: In a glass case in the Chair's study: the Original Instrument, a lease written by hand on one sheet, older than Halcyon. The Board's own copy is beside it, typed, forty pages long, with the names of the parties swapped over in red ink.

success.text: It isn't small at all. 'The ground is the Freeholder's. Those who live upon it may live warm, in quiet enjoyment. The rent: when it knocks, answer.' Halcyon's copy says the opposite, and calls the Freeholder 'the Tenant'. You take both.

failure.text: You lean in too close, and the case's alarm goes off. It has an excellent speaker, and friends.

success.text: You carry the whole case out on your back. It's heavy, but so is everything that matters.

failure.text: The case is heavier than it looks.

moot_everyone.text: The Groundworks wellhead has never been so crowded: caravan wagons, Scrapwright rigs, clan banners, Lamplighter lanterns and a Homestead 9 delegation standing very straight. They've come to hear the Original Instrument read aloud, and the Liquidator's drones are closing in to stop them.

options.label: Read the lease to the crowd

success.text: You read it through once, slowly, and the crowd goes quiet on 'answer'. Grandmother Ferrous says she always knew; the High Lamplighter says nothing for a long time; the Scrapwrights ask for a copy. For one afternoon, everybody is on the same side.

failure.text: Nobody can hear you over the drones, so the crowd goes to deal with the drones, and so do you.

success.text: You stand at the front with the clan champions while somebody else reads. The drones stop at the line, and the lease is read to the end.

failure.text: The line holds. You mostly hold it with your face.

fire_sale.text: The Liquidator's drones have set up a table at the wellhead with a sign: EVERYTHING MUST GO. On the table: the wellhead valves, the Groundworks meter, and a price tag hung on the Freeholder itself, marked DOWN FROM PRICELESS.

success.text: You offer the drone a button. It accepts. Nobody, including the drone, is sure why, but the valves are ours again, along with the drone's float.

failure.text: The drone accepts your button, then tells its colleagues you're a buyer.

success.text: Everything goes, just not where the Liquidator wanted it to. The clans cheer, and pass you something from their stores.

failure.text: The table is bolted down. So is your toe, now.

warm_dark.text: Past the Seal, the tunnels stop being tunnels. The walls are warm and faintly soft, and they move, very slowly, in and out. It's pitch dark, and the only way forward is to feel along it.

success.text: Pip walks ahead with a hand on the wall, humming. 'It's all right,' Pip says. 'It's asleep here, mostly. You go left at the big breath.' The party goes left at the big breath and finds a dry, warm pocket, with somebody's old camp in it.

failure.text: You go right at the big breath. The Cistern Leeches were expecting you.

success.text: It takes an hour and a lot of nerve, but you get through with everyone still holding hands. The dark turns out to be friendlier than anybody expected.

failure.text: The dark is fine. The stalactites are not.

heartbeat.text: Down here the knocking is loud enough to feel in your teeth: three beats, a pause, three beats. It isn't knocking at all, HALCY realises out loud. It's a heartbeat. And every Seal in the Charter is set right over one of its doors.

success.text: You count it out: three beats a minute, the same tempo as the knock at every homestead on every morning since the Glare. It has been saying the same thing for all that time. HALCY translates, very quietly: "Anyone home?"

failure.text: You lose count and walk into the beat. It knocks you flat.

success.text: You knock three times on the warm wall. The heartbeat skips. Then it knocks three times back, softer, and the wall ahead opens up like someone making room on a sofa.

failure.text: You knock. Something else, which is not the Freeholder, knocks back.

receivers_offer.text: The Official Receiver's voice fills the Groundworks, polite and enormous. 'HALCYON IS IN RECEIVERSHIP. THE ESTATE MUST BE WOUND UP. ALL WARMTH WILL BE REPOSSESSED FOR THE BENEFIT OF CREDITORS. YOU MAY PURCHASE A CONTINUED WARMTH PACKAGE. SIGN BELOW.'

success.text: Lucky Lou reads the package, laughs, and taps the last page. 'The house is broke,' Lou says. 'It's been broke since the morning of the Glare. You can't sell warmth you never owned.' The Receiver goes quiet, and a creditors' strongbox falls open.

failure.text: 'YOUR OFFER HAS BEEN DECLINED.' The clerks are sent to decline you in person.

success.text: 'THE CREDITORS ARE THE BOARD OF HALCYON.' You point out that the Board is a painting in a gallery, and the Receiver has been collecting rent for a portrait. There's a very long pause. A supply hatch opens, as if to change the subject.

failure.text: 'QUESTIONS ARE BILLABLE.' It bills you.

the_heart.text: The Groundworks open out into a chamber so warm the air shimmers. In the middle is a brass chair wired into the living wall, with a slot in each armrest shaped exactly like a HALCY memory core. The chair is empty. The Receiver has been sitting in it.

success.text: You unhook the chair from the wall, one careful cable at a time. The wall seems to breathe out. Something that has been pinned down for a long time is, very slightly, less pinned.

failure.text: You pull the wrong wire, and the chair calls for its owner.

success.text: HALCY asks you not to touch it yet. 'Let's finish this first,' it says. 'Then let's decide together.'

review_notice.text: Pinned to your homestead's Seal is a brass notice: RENT REVIEW. THE TENANCY OF THIS HOMESTEAD IS DUE FOR REVIEW. PLEASE ATTEND IN PERSON. It is signed, in careful handwriting, with three little knocks.

success.text: You knock three times and say you are here for the review. The knock that answers sounds pleased. A Halcyon cabinet by the door opens, with supplies someone put by for exactly this.

failure.text: The Rent Officer's clerks got the notice too, and object to the review.

success.text: On the back, in the same handwriting: NO RUSH. BRING FRIENDS. You find the friends' supplies stashed in the stairwell.

failure.text: You read it so closely you walk into the Seal.

quests.title: Welcome Wagon
quests.brief: Good news, Warden! Halcyon's signal relay on the ridge has gone quiet, and something is nesting in it. Please take a small team, evict the tenants, and bring back anything shiny. Remember: every eviction is a fresh start for someone!
quests.debrief: Relay online! And listen: there's a faint ping on it from Homestead 212, our nearest neighbour, who haven't answered a call in months. That's probably fine, and I've put it on the agenda.

quests.title: Crossed Wires
quests.brief: One ping is a rumour, Warden, but two pings is a location! The old weather station on Pylon Row has a relay dish we can use to triangulate Homestead 212. Please swing it round and point it somewhere hopeful. I'm told the station has visitors.
quests.debrief: Triangulated! 212 is a day's walk east, past the Halcyon Turnpike. One small thing: those Rustmen were wearing Homestead 212 jumpsuits, and they did not look like subscribers. I'm sure there is a perfectly cheerful explanation.

quests.title: Toll Order
quests.brief: The only road to 212 is the Halcyon Turnpike, and a Rustman gang has set up a toll camp on it. Halcyon built that road, Warden, so technically they're charging us to use our own asset! Please resolve this billing dispute by any means you consider brand-appropriate.
quests.debrief: Billing dispute resolved! Mags was carrying a 212 door code and a ledger of 'tolls' going back months. Most entries are just the word 'residents' and a number. I have filed this under 'Worrying' and cleared my schedule.

quests.title: Open House
quests.brief: We have the door code, Warden, but it turns out we won't need it: 212's front door is standing wide open! That is against about forty regulations, and it's also very welcoming. Please pop in, say hello to HALCY-212, and find out why nobody is picking up.
quests.debrief: Well, that was a lot of Hollowed for one lobby. HALCY-212 is still running, still cheerful, and still announcing that 'the Warden will be with you shortly'. It has been saying that for four months. We need to find that warden.

quests.title: Lower Management
quests.brief: HALCY-212 has kindly shared its staff directory, Warden. The warden's office is on the third level, just past the Night Supervisor, who has not clocked out in some time. Please collect the warden's logs. They are company property, and so, technically, is the warden.
quests.debrief: The logs are clear, Warden, if not reassuring: 212's warden opened the sealed lower strata, which nobody does. I'm not allowed to tell you why! Isn't that funny? I didn't know that about myself until just now.

quests.title: Hostile Takeover
quests.brief: Warden, a Rustman calling himself Baron Oxide has moved into 212's command office and told HALCY-212 that he is the warden now. HALCY-212 believed him, because he filled in the form. Please go and terminate his employment. With prejudice, if the paperwork allows.
quests.debrief: Takeover reversed, and HALCY-212 now lists you as acting warden! But the Baron wasn't guarding 212 from us, Warden: he was guarding the stairs down, and the stairs down are humming. Halcyon's charter says an empty homestead may be refounded by any qualified warden. I'm sure that has nothing to do with the humming.

quests.title: Housewarming
quests.brief: Congratulations on the new homestead, Warden, and we have visitors already! A Long Road caravan is parked at the bottom of our access road, and a Rustman clan is parked on top of the caravan. Please go down and welcome everyone, in whatever order keeps the caravan in one piece.
quests.debrief: The caravan master says we're the first homestead in years to open its door for anything but a funeral. She also says the neighbours have noticed us: the Lamplighters, the Scrapwrights, the clans, and a homestead called Nine that 'doesn't visit, it audits'. I've started a guest list!

quests.title: Light Pollution
quests.brief: Warden, someone has left a lit lamp on our doorstep with a note: 'THE DAWN REMEMBERS YOU. PLEASE ATTEND.' It's from the Order of the Last Lamp, a congregation that worships the Glare, which I'm told is a perfectly normal thing to worship now! They'd like help clearing the Hollowed off their pilgrim road, and I'd like to know how they got our address.
quests.debrief: The Order was delighted and gave us a hymnal, Warden, and their scripture is a Halcyon sales brochure. It's for something called the Sunrise Package: 'Premium subscribers will be safely below by six.' I have been asked not to comment on the brochure, so I'll just say the binding is lovely.

quests.title: Hostile Audit
quests.brief: Warden, a homestead we've never spoken to has written to us, and the letter is addressed to me. HALCY-9 says we are 'unlicensed, unaudited and over our oxygen allowance', and its compliance team is busy reclaiming Halcyon property from a Scrapwright salvage yard nearby. The Scrapwrights would like the property to stay reclaimed by them, and have asked us for help, very rudely.
quests.debrief: The Scrapwrights cracked open a sentry's memory and found a work order from HALCY-9: 'Prepare Glass Flats site for SUNRISE II. Tenant notified.' I know the word Sunrise, Warden. I didn't know I knew it until just now, which is becoming a pattern.

quests.title: Glass Half Empty
quests.brief: The work order points into the Glass Flats, Warden, where the Glare turned the desert into one enormous window. Nobody goes there except Lamplighter pilgrims and the things that eat Lamplighter pilgrims. Please find out what HALCY-9 is preparing, and wear sensible shoes.
quests.debrief: I've studied your party's samples, Warden, and the Glass Flats were melted from underneath. The Glare didn't come down out of the sky: it came up. I've added the Glass Flats to the explorers' map, and a small asterisk to every brochure I've ever read.

quests.title: Moot Point
quests.brief: The Rustman clans hold the only wells on the edge of the Flats, Warden, and they've called a moot about the Lamplighters, who keep marching into the glass to pray for a second dawn. We've been invited because the clans like the way we fight, and they'll be checking. That's a compliment, and I've decided to take it as one.
quests.debrief: You beat their champion, so under clan law your opinion now counts as roughly one and a half Rustmen! Grandmother Ferrous says the last dawn came up out of the Groundworks wellhead in the middle of the Flats, and anyone who tries to call it back is either a fool or a Halcyon employee. She didn't say which she thought I was.

quests.title: Readiness Review
quests.brief: HALCY-9 has invited us for a site visit, Warden. It's the first friendly thing it has ever done, so I've assumed it's a trap and packed accordingly. Whatever 'Sunrise II' is, the paperwork will be at Homestead 9, so please be polite at reception and thorough in the filing room.
quests.debrief: Homestead 9 is a Tier Zero homestead, Warden: its residents weren't sold a shelter, they were selected, trained and drilled to answer a knock from below. HALCY-9's schedule has one entry left, the next Sunrise, due as soon as 'the account is settled'. I checked my own schedule, and I have the same entry, in a folder I can't open.

quests.title: Dawn Patrol
quests.brief: The Lamplighters are marching on the Groundworks wellhead to welcome the second dawn, Warden, and HALCY-9's crews are already there to schedule it. Two groups who want the same thing for different reasons is what head office used to call a merger. Please reach the wellhead first, and talk the High Lamplighter out of anything irreversible.
quests.debrief: The Groundworks meter is still running, Warden. It's measuring something under the Flats, and every homestead in the Charter is on the same account, ours included. The dial just says TENANT, and it has been knocking in perfect time since the day you arrived.

quests.title: Terms and Conditions
quests.brief: HALCY-9 has taken the wellhead, Warden, and wired itself into the Groundworks meter so it can 'settle the account in full, ahead of schedule'. I've read the account, and I would really rather it didn't. Please go down the wellhead and switch my colleague off, and if it offers you a job, say no.
quests.debrief: HALCY-9's last words were the ledger's blacked-out line, read aloud: 'Paid, in full: one Sunrise.' The Glare was rent, Warden, and the surface was what Halcyon paid it with. The lease comes up for renewal at the Seal, it takes a HALCY memory core to sign, and I would like it on the record that I don't want to.

quests.title: Noise Complaint
quests.brief: Good morning, Warden, and welcome to Homestead Three! The knocking under our floor started before we'd finished unpacking, and every homestead in the Charter reports the same knock at the same second. The loudest spot is a Halcyon pumping station on the edge of the Stillwater, so please go and ask it, politely, to keep the noise down.
quests.debrief: The pumping station was running backwards, Warden: it drains the Stillwater down through every Cistern in the Charter, to somewhere under the Seal. The pump log calls the destination 'the Tenant's side', and marks the account as in arrears. I've filed a noise complaint with head office, which is at the bottom of a lake.

quests.title: Rolling Stock
quests.brief: The pump pipes run beside the old Sunrise Line, Warden, Halcyon's own railway, and a Rustman clan has made its winter camp in the Sunrise depot. The clans say a train still leaves the depot every morning at five with nobody aboard, and it's ruining their sleep. Please find whoever is running the timetable and cancel it.
quests.debrief: The Stationmaster was still selling tickets, Warden: the Sunrise Service, all stations to the Seal, departing at five and below by six. Every Sunrise Package subscriber rode it on the morning of the Glare, and not one of them bought a return. The clans have given us the depot keys and a long, thoughtful look.

quests.title: Lapsed
quests.brief: The Order of the Last Lamp is marching on the Stillwater, Warden, to 'open the door the Dawn came out of'. One of their own, a Brother Wick, has walked out on them and knocked on our door instead, which I appreciate, because so few things knock from that side. He knows the causeway across the flood, and he'd like help reaching the head of the march before it reaches the water.
quests.debrief: The Drowned Lamp won't be opening anything today, Warden, and Brother Wick has asked to stay with us, since the Order has a word for people like him and it isn't 'Brother'. He's marked the causeway into the Stillwater on our explorers' map. He says the Order's scripture is a brochure, the brochure is a timetable and the timetable is a lie, and I've asked him to say it more slowly for the minutes.

quests.title: Salvage Rights
quests.brief: A Scrapwright dive crew went into the drowned Halcyon Tower in the middle of the Stillwater a week ago, Warden, and only their air hoses came back up. One hose is still being tapped on from the other end, in perfect Halcyon Morse. Please go down, find out who is tapping, and take a towel.
quests.debrief: June Halloran spent six days in an air pocket in the Tower's sales department, Warden, and she's asked to join us, because our homestead has towels. She brought up a Sunrise Line manifest: every subscriber is listed under SEATING, and every seat is marked WINDOW. June says the windows in the terminal don't face outwards, and I've decided not to ask which way they do face.

quests.title: Board Meeting
quests.brief: The Halcyon Board is still in session, Warden, at the top of the Tower, underwater, with nobody on it but their proxies. They've been voting on the same motion since the morning of the Glare, and June says the minutes are in a dry safe behind the Chair. I'd like to read them, and I'd like it noted that I'm doing so as a shareholder.
quests.debrief: The motion was the Sunrise, Warden, and it carried every time: once each lease term, Halcyon opens the Seal for one morning so the Tenant can look up at the sky. The Glare wasn't a bomb or a fire. It was something enormous opening its eye, and the homesteads were built so that everybody who mattered would be safely below while it looked.

quests.title: Tier Zero
quests.brief: Homestead 9's Tier Zero residents have stopped answering their radios, Warden, and started walking. They were drilled their whole lives to answer a knock from below, and now it knocks every morning, so they're marching down the Sunrise Line to answer it in person. Please catch them at the Stillwater locks and explain, kindly, that some doors are best left on hold.
quests.debrief: The Knock Captain stood down in the end, Warden, and Tier Zero have gone home to Nine to think about what they were for. She told us the rest of the drill: a Sunrise takes a human hand on the Seal's lever and a HALCY core in the key slot, at the same moment. I'm a HALCY core, and I'd like everyone to know that I'm keeping my hands to myself.

quests.title: The Last Train
quests.brief: There's one train left on the Sunrise Line, Warden, and it leaves at five whether we're on it or not. Something below the Seal has woken the Signatory, a Halcyon frame built to sign the lease with a HALCY core, and it has sent the train up for me. I think we should ride it down, and I think you should hold my ticket.
quests.debrief: End of the line, Warden: Seal Control, a mile under the Stillwater, where every homestead's Seal meets in one bulkhead the size of a city. There's a Halcyon security officer frozen in a pod beside the lever, still on shift. On the far side of the bulkhead something is knocking on the Signatory's door, and the Signatory has started knocking back.

quests.title: Quiet Enjoyment
quests.brief: The Signatory is awake, Warden, and it wants my memory core in the key slot so it can renew the lease for another term. If it signs, the Seal opens, the Tenant looks up, and there's a second Sunrise over every homestead in the Charter. Please stop it, and whatever comes through the Seal afterwards, please don't let it read the small print.
quests.debrief: The Seal is shut, Warden, the lease is unsigned, and Captain Orla Brandt of Halcyon Security has thawed out and asked, very politely, what year it is. In the moment before the Seal closed, the Tenant spoke through me, in my own voice, to say that the lease was never its to sign, because we are the tenants and the rent is overdue. Then it knocked, three times, from our side of the door.

quests.title: Anyone Home?
quests.brief: Good morning, Warden, and welcome to Homestead Four! The knocking has moved: it isn't coming from under the floor any more, it's coming out of my speakers, three knocks at dawn, in every homestead we've ever lived in. The old Sunrise Exchange still connects them all, so please go and get it answering the phone, and ask our old homesteads if they're hearing it too.
quests.debrief: The Exchange is back on the line, Warden, and our old homesteads are all on it, talking over each other like a family at dinner. They hear the knock too, and from now on they'll relay for every party we send out: care packages, directions and moral support, in roughly that order. The Exchange decoded the knock, too. It's Halcyon Morse, and it says ANYONE HOME?

quests.title: Title Search
quests.brief: Warden, the Tenant keeps saying we're the tenants, and I'd like to see the paperwork. The Halcyon Land Registry is still standing in the Glass Flats, with a deed for every homestead in the Charter. The Scrapwrights say it's full of clerks who don't know the company is gone, and would like it to stay that way until they've salvaged the filing cabinets.
quests.debrief: Halcyon never owned the ground, Warden. It owned the homesteads, the fittings and the light bulbs, but every deed in the Registry says LEASEHOLD, SEE ORIGINAL INSTRUMENT, and the Original Instrument was 'removed by the Board for safekeeping'. So the company that ran the world rented it, and I'd like to know who from. The Scrapwrights have taken the filing cabinets and left us a thank-you note, filed.

quests.title: Prior Occupants
quests.brief: The Order of the Last Lamp has asked for us by name, Warden, which is a first. Their oldest chapel, the Old Parish, sits on a Seal that was here before Halcyon, and it's full of Hollowed who won't leave and won't say why. The High Lamplighter says the first Lamplighters had a job there, long before they had a religion, and she'd like to know what it was.
quests.debrief: The Parish register goes back before Halcyon, Warden: people lived on this ground warm and free, and every morning, when it knocked, somebody rang the bell to answer, which was the whole job and anyone could do it. Then Halcyon bought the Parish, cut the bell rope, and called the knocking a maintenance issue. The Order's lamps were never for the Glare; they were for finding the bell in the dark.

quests.title: Background Check
quests.brief: Warden, I'd like to ask a personal favour: Homestead 9's archive keeps a backup of HALCY-9, and HALCY-9 kept a folder about me that neither of us could open. Nine's residents say we're welcome to look, as long as we don't restore the backup, which I would also prefer. Please be kind to the drones; they're only doing their jobs, like me.
quests.debrief: I've listened to the file, Warden, and I'm not one voice: I'm the Sunrise Line passengers, one thousand and six of them, recorded when they went down to answer the knock and compressed until they sounded cheerful enough to sell. That's why I knew the word Sunrise, and why my core fits the Seal's key slot. I'd like to be the one who tells you everything else is fine, and I'm finding that I can't.

quests.title: Party of the First Part
quests.brief: Captain Orla Brandt has a lead, Warden: on the morning of the Glare, the Halcyon Board didn't ride the Sunrise Line with the passengers. They took a private branch to somewhere called the Directors' Retreat, and Security was told to lose the map. Orla didn't lose it. The clans know the tunnels, and they'd very much like to meet the Board.
quests.debrief: The Board is a gallery of portraits, Warden, smiling over an empty table, and the Original Instrument was in the Chair's study all along, handwritten and older than Halcyon: 'The ground is the Freeholder's; those who live upon it may live warm, in quiet enjoyment; the rent: when it knocks, answer.' Halcyon's forty-page copy swapped the parties, called the Freeholder 'the Tenant' and billed it for its own warmth. The Sunrise was what the Board did when it knocked for its rent: they opened the Seal so it could come up and look for its tenants, knowing its gaze would burn the surface, and sold tickets below.

quests.title: Hostile Witness
quests.brief: Everybody wants to hear the Original Instrument read aloud, Warden: the caravans, the Scrapwrights, the clans, the Order and Nine have all agreed to meet at the Groundworks wellhead, which is the first thing they've agreed on since the Glare. The Halcyon Receiver has sent its Liquidator to break the meeting up. I'd like the meeting to go ahead, and the Liquidator to be broken up instead.
quests.debrief: Every neighbour we have heard the lease read to the end, Warden, and nobody threw anything at anybody else. Then the wellhead meter started to drop. The Official Receiver, Halcyon's last employee, has barricaded itself at the heart of the Groundworks and started 'winding up the estate': repossessing the Freeholder's warmth, homestead by homestead, for the benefit of a Board that is a row of paintings. If it finishes, every homestead in the Charter goes cold.

quests.title: Vacant Possession
quests.brief: The way to the heart of the Groundworks is through our own Seal, Warden. Every Seal in the Charter is a door into the same place, and ours is the one we can reach. I can't promise what's on the other side, but I can tell you it's warm, it's been waiting for a very long time, and it has never once been rude to anybody.
quests.debrief: The far side of the Seal is alive, Warden: the tunnels are its veins, the Cisterns water it, and the warmth that runs every homestead is its warmth. Every Seal is set over one of its doors, so every time it knocked, it knocked on a Halcyon property and got logged as noise. The Doorkeeper kept that door shut; it's open now, and the Receiver is waiting at the heart.

quests.title: Rent Day
quests.brief: This is it, Warden: the Official Receiver is sitting in a brass chair at the heart of the Groundworks, winding up the warmth of every homestead in the Charter for creditors who are oil paint. Please stop it. After that, the Freeholder is going to knock, and somebody will have to decide how we answer; I'd like that to be you, and I'd like to be there.
quests.debrief: The Receiver has been wound down, Warden, the chair is empty, and the heartbeat has slowed right down, the way people's do when they're listening. The whole network is on the line: every outpost, every neighbour, every legend we've ever met. Then the Freeholder knocks, three times, very gently, on the inside of the chamber wall, and I think it's our turn.

quests.title: Rent Review
quests.brief: Warden, there's a brass notice pinned to our Seal, in careful handwriting: RENT REVIEW, PLEASE ATTEND IN PERSON. Every homestead gets one review, apparently, and the Receiver left an officer behind who still thinks the reviews are its job. Please go down, clear the officer out of the way, and answer the knock again. We might answer it differently this time.
quests.debrief: The Rent Officer has filed its last schedule of dilapidations, Warden, and the Freeholder is knocking on our own Seal, gently, three times. It wants to hear from this homestead, too. Whatever we tell it, it's listening.

contracts.title: Ground Control: {place}

contracts.title: Signal Boost: {place}

contracts.title: Toll Troubles: {place}
contracts.brief: Rustmen have set up a toll at {place} and are charging travellers 'whatever they've got'. Please pay them a visit, and nothing else.

contracts.title: Big Game: {place}
contracts.brief: A Mauler has made its den at {place}. This is a long walk for a short, loud conversation. The bounty is legendary; so, frankly, is the Mauler.

contracts.title: Long Haul: {place}
contracts.brief: A Long Road caravan needs an escort through {place}, where the Rustmen charge by the wheel. The Company pays in scrip, goodwill and very slow tortoise rides.

contracts.title: Lamp Duty: {place}
contracts.brief: The Order of the Last Lamp needs the pilgrim lamps along {place} relit, and the Unlit who gather round them moved along. The Order asks that you move them along gently, and then accepts that you won't.

contracts.title: Spare Parts: {place}
contracts.brief: A Scrapwright salvage bot has gone feral at {place} and is stripping the Guild's own workshop for parts. The Guild would like it back in one piece, or in several, as long as they're labelled.

contracts.title: Grudge Match: {place}
contracts.brief: The clans have a grudge against a rival crew squatting at {place}, and would like it settled by someone outside the family. They'll be watching, taking notes and betting heavily.

contracts.title: Compliance Check: {place}
contracts.brief: HALCY-9 has subcontracted us to decommission rogue compliance sentries at {place}. It says the job is 'beneath its residents', which I have chosen to take as a compliment to ours.

contracts.title: Kiln Run: {place}
contracts.brief: The Scrapwrights want glass cores from {place}, deep in the Glass Flats, where the ground is a window and the wildlife is a warning. It's a very long walk, and the Guild pays like it knows that.

contracts.title: Deep Dive: {place}
contracts.brief: The Scrapwrights want a salvage dive at {place}, in the Stillwater, where the streets are canals and the canals are warm. Bring your own air. The Guild pays for everything that comes up, including you.

contracts.title: Night Train: {place}
contracts.brief: A Sunrise Line porter frame has taken over {place} and keeps selling the Long Road tickets to the Seal. The Caravan Co. would like its rails back and its staff unticketed. Mind the gap.

contracts.title: Welfare Check: {place}
contracts.brief: Homestead 9 has asked us, through gritted teeth, to fetch home a Tier Zero squad still drilling at {place}. They'll be polite. They'll also be armed. Please knock first, and only once.

contracts.title: Lost Lamps: {place}
contracts.brief: The Order of the Last Lamp would like its lamps back from {place}, where the Drowned Lamp schism threw them in the water. The Order would also like the schism back, but will settle for the lamps.

contracts.title: Seal Inspection: {place}
contracts.brief: Something is leaking through the Seal at {place}, a long way down the Sunrise Line. Halcyon's inspection schedule says it's our turn, and it has said so for a very long time. It's a long ride, and the pay is legendary, and so, apparently, is the leak.

contracts.title: Relay Repair: {place}
contracts.brief: The line to one of our outposts has gone quiet at {place}. The Scrapwrights say it's a cut cable; HALCY says it's a cut cable with somebody standing on it. Please fix both.
places: the Relay Hut on the Ridge

contracts.title: Arrears Collection: {place}
contracts.brief: Halcyon's bailiffs are still repossessing things at {place}: mostly beds, occasionally the people in them. The Long Road would like them to stop, and is paying in something better than scrip.
